chapter: Trummy Young's band, 52nd Street and the Navy
title: Discharged after eight days and sent home
summary: The Navy decides he serves better as a civilian, and he surprises his wife by returning.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Finally, after a question-and-answer period of about 35 minutes, they told me to go back to my barracks, and they would contact me later. I went back to the barracks, and in a couple of days I was summoned to go back to this (?) place. They said, "Well, John, we've made a decision. We feel that

you would do a better service to your country as a civilian than you would as a sailor." So I didn't say anything. They said something like, "What do you think about that?" I said, "Whatever you say, sir" or something like that. I didn't want to express what I was feeling! All I wanted to do was get the hell out of that door, boy. Anyway, they said, "We'll say that everything is taken care of."

Anyway, I went back and... The day that I went in there was a Friday, and the next Saturday they gave me my ticket home and told me to go straight home, that I was under the Navy's care until I got to my door. And my stint in the Navy was eight days.

So I came back home, and I like to scared my wife to death because she had no idea she was going to see me that soon! I just told her, "Well, it must have been your prayers," because actually it was just a series of circumstances that... It was just almost like telling somebody what they wanted to hear. They asked the questions and I answered them, and obviously it was the right time and everything. Because I know so many other guys who tried things to get out, and nothing worked!
